name: cascade-desktop
description: Cascade, Debate 101's keyboard-first flowing app — desktop shell around the flow/ web app.
//: electron-builder reads the 'build' key below. See build/README.md for icon setup.

build.//files: Only the desktop shell code goes inside the app bundle/asar. The web app itself ships via extraResources below, not this list, because it needs to sit on plain disk (not inside the asar) so the app:// protocol handler in main.js can read it with plain fs calls at a predictable, resolveable path.
build.//extraResources: This is how /flow ships inside the desktop app. electron-builder copies '../flow' (resolved relative to THIS file, i.e. the repo's flow/ directory — the same one served at https://debate101.org/flow/) into the packaged app's resources directory, unpacked (not zipped into app.asar), under a 'flow' subfolder. main.js resolves that same folder two different ways depending on whether it's running from source or from a build: in dev, __dirname is .../desktop, so the flow dir is path.join(__dirname, '..', 'flow'); once packaged, extraResources always lands at process.resourcesPath (Contents/Resources on mac, resources/ on win & linux), so the flow dir is path.join(process.resourcesPath, 'flow'). Both paths are computed in main.js's resolveFlowDir().
build.//fileAssociations: Registers the .ebb double-click-to-open behavior on all three platforms. This top-level block is the cross-platform baseline (electron-builder turns it into Windows registry entries, a Linux .desktop MimeType line, and — on its own — a basic mac CFBundleDocumentTypes entry). The mac.extendInfo block below layers a proper Uniform Type Identifier on top so Spotlight/QuickLook/Finder treat .ebb as a first-class, well-described type instead of a bare extension match.

mac.//hardenedRuntime: Required by Apple for notarization. It is turned on here so the config is ready the day a paid Apple Developer certificate exists — but identity is forced to null below, which tells electron-builder to skip code signing entirely for local/CI builds run without a certificate. An unsigned, non-notarized .app still runs; macOS Gatekeeper just blocks the first double-click launch (see desktop/README.md for the right-click > Open workaround). Flip identity to a real 'Developer ID Application: ...' string (or delete the override) once signing is set up.

dmg.//sign: The dmg wrapper image itself doesn't need signing even when the .app inside does; keep it off so a no-certificate build doesn't fail trying.

linux.//mimeTypes: Belt-and-suspenders alongside fileAssociations[].mimeType above — this is the field electron-builder documents specifically for adding extra MIME types to the generated .desktop entry.
